title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1969-01-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough‑sounding soundboard captures a fiery 1969 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star and ferocious Garcia solo, despite a clanky bass‑drum pedal.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its high energy jams – Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven > Death Don't Have No Mercy and the sprawling Other One sequence are repeatedly called out as classics, with Jerry’s solo described as earth‑shattering. The recording is a vintage soundboard that suffers from an overly loud bass‑drum pedal, occasional cuts and a bit of hiss, but most listeners feel the musical fire outweighs those flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently rated very high (many 4‑5★ comments on jams and solos) while recording quality is noted as good but marred by a clanky bass drum and occasional glitches; the weighted average yields ~4.2★.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear vintage soundboard with minimal hiss, but plagued by an overly loud, clanky bass‑drum pedal, occasional splices/cuts and a few dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, evolving jam sequence (Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death Don't) builds into a powerful second half with Cryptical Envelopment, Drums, The Other One and finishes with Cosmic Charlie, delivering high‑energy flow despite a hesitant start.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Ferocious, earth‑shattering solo praised; described as fierce and brilliant.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass patterns during The Eleven and The Other One highlighted; noted for “tree‑trunk pick” tone and overall strong contribution despite occasional drunkenness.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal harmonies appreciated; no specific guitar commentary beyond general praise.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s bass‑drum pedal is excessively loud and clanky, a recurring technical complaint.
